title: XamlKeys JSON report
description: The shape written by --json. schemaVersion only increases on a major release; new fields may be added without bumping it, so consumers must ignore fields they do not recognise.

summary.description: Counts, and — just as important — what this run could not see.

dialectMixed.description: The tree holds both WPF and WinUI projects, whose merge order is opposite. Each dictionary was resolved with its own project's rules.

coverage.description: Share of merged dictionaries that could be read. Below minCoverage the run exits 3, because 'unused' cannot be trusted.

suppressed.description: Hidden by ignore comments, config or a baseline.

unresolvedSites.description: References whose key is not a string (x:Type, x:Static).

invalidIgnores.description: Ignore comments with no reason. They suppress nothing.

dynamicKeySites.description: C# lookups that build the key at runtime.

frameworkKeyOverrides.description: Keys that redefine a framework-provided key (WinUI lightweight styling, System* resources). The framework's own templates read them, so they are never reported as unused.

unusedOnlyViaUnused.description: How many of the unused findings are keys referenced only from inside other unused resources (counted in 'unused' as well).

keysNamedInCode.description: Further keys counted as used because their exact name appears as an ordinary string (not a lookup argument) in the same project's C#, for example handed to a helper method. Never reported as unused.

dynamicKeysNamedInCode.description: DynamicResource/ThemeResource references whose key no XAML defines but whose name (or a name plus a composed suffix such as $"{x}75") appears as a string in C# -- keys added to resources at runtime. Not reported as dangling.

keysMatchingComposedWrites.description: References whose key starts with a fixed prefix (three characters or more) that C# in the same or a related project composes resource keys from when writing them (Resources["Language_" + key] = value, Resources.Add($"Language_{key}", value)). Not reported as dangling: the keys exist at run time, typically strings read from a non-XAML file.

keysAddedInCode.description: References to a key no XAML defines but C# adds to resources in the same or a related project (Resources.Add("K", ...), Resources.Add(nameof(K), ...), Resources["K"] = ...). Not reported as dangling, StaticResource included: adding before InitializeComponent() is a valid way to define a key.

keysResolvedThroughHosts.description: DynamicResource references in a UserControl (an x:Class file) whose key is not in the control's own scope but is in scope at every place the control is put in XAML in the same or a related project, following hosts that are themselves placed controls. Not reported as out-of-scope. Not applied when C# also creates the control (new X(), typeof(X), <X>) or to StaticResource, which resolves before the control is placed.

keysFromControlResources.description: References written on (or inside) an element whose class is an x:Class file in this tree, resolved in that class's own root resources -- the instance's resources are filled in its constructor. Not reported as out-of-scope.

conditionalAlternatives.description: Keys defined more than once in one dictionary under complementary conditional-XAML namespaces (http://...presentation?IsApiContractPresent(X) and ?IsApiContractNotPresent(X)). Only one of them exists at runtime, so they are not reported as duplicate keys or shadowing.

inlineDictionaryKeys.description: Keys in a <ResourceDictionary> element that is not under any Resources property or MergedDictionaries -- for example the dictionaries of a chart Palette (WPF/Silverlight Toolkit). Such a dictionary is its own scope; its keys are read by that control by convention and are not reported as unused.

placedTeachingTips.description: WinUI TeachingTip elements placed in a Resources dictionary -- the documented way to attach a tip without taking layout space; they open through their own IsOpen, not by a key lookup. Not reported as unused.

dictionariesCreatedInCode.description: Dictionaries with an x:Class that C# in the same or a related project creates with new X() (for example MergedDictionaries.Add(new DarkTheme())). Not reported as orphans. Where they are merged is not known, so their keys are not added to any scope.

keysUsedAsFields.description: Resources named with x:Name whose name appears as a word in the XAML file's code-behind (X.xaml.cs, X.cs, X.xaml.cpp/.h, X.cpp/.h) -- used as a generated field or C++/WinRT accessor, not looked up by string. Not reported as unused.

shadowedButResolvedByStatic.description: Definitions that a later merged dictionary overrides but that a {StaticResource} in their own dictionary resolves to at load time (each control theme file keeping its own copy of a key). Not reported as shadowed: they do win for those references. DynamicResource references do not count -- they resolve at run time to the merged winner.

layeredOverrides.description: Definitions that one theme overrides by including them and redefining the key (a Windows 11 theme over a Windows 10 base) but that win in another root dictionary which uses them directly, or that are overridden only by an optional keyed dictionary selected at runtime (Avalonia's density styles). Not reported as shadowed: they are not 'never used'.

startupResources.description: Keyed resources in App.xaml whose element is a *Bootstrapper (Caliburn.Micro's <local:Bootstrapper x:Key="bootstrapper"/>). Nothing references them; they exist to be created at startup. Not reported as unused.

keyedDictionaries.description: Keyed ResourceDictionaries nested in a dictionary (<ResourceDictionary x:Key="Compact">). Treated as mutually exclusive alternatives the app merges at runtime; their keys count as defined.

libraryKeyOverrides.description: Keys that belong to a library and are redefined to restyle it: a library key overridden by another project of this tree (not reported as shadowed: the library's definition still wins for other consumers), or a {x:Static}/{ComponentResourceKey} key whose type is not in this tree's C# (that library's own templates read it; not reported as unused).

classBackedDictionaries.description: Dictionaries or Avalonia style files merged as an element (<local:MyTheme/>) whose class is defined by an x:Class file in this tree. Resolved instead of counted as external.

keysMatchingComposedLookups.description: Keys counted as used because they match the fixed start and end of a key C# composes at runtime ($"Icon{name}", "Icon" + name), within the same project. Never reported as unused.

keysNamedNearDynamicLookups.description: Keys counted as used because their name appears as a string literal in a C# file that looks resources up by variable. Never reported as unused.

libraryKeysNotChecked.description: Keys in library projects, not evaluated for usage.

unusedDefinitions.description: Definitions covered by the unused findings (one finding per key name).

knownThemeSources.description: Merged theme sources the tool cannot read but whose key names it knows from a bundled list (WinUI's XamlControlsResources, Avalonia's FluentTheme/SimpleTheme/ColorPicker/DataGrid/TreeDataGrid themes, CommunityToolkit for WinUI, .NET's WPF Fluent theme). Counted as resolved in coverage; a key not on the list is still reported as external.

themePacksInUse.description: Optional key lists that apply to this tree because it merges that theme: wpf-fluent, avalonia-fluent, avalonia-fluent2, avalonia-simple, avalonia-colorpicker, avalonia-datagrid, avalonia-treedatagrid, community-toolkit.

counts.description: Per-kind counts. Keys are camelCase here; findings[].kind uses the kebab-case form.

file.description: Relative to the scan root, forward slashes.

related.description: The other end: the winner of a shadowing, the first of a duplicate, the definition an out-of-scope reference wanted.
